21	## Problem
22	
23	docs/archive/cosim_roi.md gives a window, for one topology only:
24	
25	1. No lock-step from reset. `--hybrid-cosim` requires `--resume-from-qemu`
26	   + marker/pc trigger, and `drain_checkpoint` needs the QEMU1 passthrough
27	   snapshot. A small testbench from a constraint-based generator has no
28	   QEMU1 leg, no markers, and no trap-free guarantee.
29	2. Window, not instruction. Localization stops at the N-insn window;
30	   narrowing is manual (re-run with smaller N), vsim only accepts an
31	   interval, and haltreq slack (0-3 retires ax45mpv, 5+ ax66) means even
32	   N=1 cannot land on every retire.

34	## Core model
35	
36	One comparison engine, two front-ends. The engine: two state streams,
37	aligned record-by-record, diffed with the existing diff_states policy;
38	first mismatch wins. vsim is the DUT, QEMU is the golden model. Memory is
39	never shared and never compared (register + CSR state only, unchanged).
40	
41	## Usage 1: lock-step (`run --mode cycle --cosim`)
42	
43	```
44	QEMU (oracle): boot -> plugin arms at entry pc -> drain BEFORE every
45	               execution attempt -> append record to <out>.ckpts -> exit
46	vsim (DUT):    boot -> arm at entry pc -> halt -> record 0 ->
47	               dcsr.step loop: step, full drain, append record ->
48	               stop at K records (K = oracle record count)
49	driver:        diff record i vs record i -> first mismatch = exact insn
50	```
51	
52	- No handoff, no shared mmap, no fast-forward. Each engine boots the same
53	  ELF on its own RAM. Arm point defaults to the ELF entry (`e_entry`);
54	  `--pc-start` overrides. Record 0 is the entry state, so a pre-entry boot
55	  divergence fails at record 0.
56	- Stepping is dcsr.step, NOT haltreq: exact one-attempt granularity, zero
57	  slack. The dcsr RMW primitive exists (resume_driver.hpp L6 prv path).
58	- Trap alignment (PM decision 1): both sides emit one record per execution
59	  ATTEMPT. QEMU exec callbacks fire pre-execution, so a trapping insn gets
60	  a callback and the handler's first insn gets the next one. A dcsr.step
61	  on a trapping insn enters debug mode at the handler entry (debug spec).
62	  Record i on both sides = state before attempt i+1, traps included.
63	  minstret is compared as data and catches any counting drift loudly.
64	- Trap CSRs are drained for real (F1) and compared: mepc, mcause, mtval,
65	  mscratch, mtvec, mie, mip, satp, plus mstatus side effects (MPP/MPIE).
66	- Run order: oracle FIRST (MHz-fast, fails fast on a bad ELF, defines the
67	  record count K), then vsim bounded to K records -- a diverged DUT cannot
68	  run away.
69	- Cost: one step = resume/halt handshake + ~70 abstract reads (+ V sweep
70	  if V). Tens of steps/s expected -> a 10k-insn testbench takes minutes.
71	  Acceptable for DV. `--cosim-interval N` remains usable as a coarse
72	  haltreq-checkpoint pass for oversized testbenches.

74	Out of scope / hard assumptions:
75	- Asynchronous interrupts: out of scope for the DEFAULT lock-step -- QEMU
76	  and RTL take them at different attempt indices by nature, so testbenches
77	  must be interrupt-free here (synchronous exceptions are fully supported).
78	  Opt-in `--cosim-async` (Usage 3, features F8-F10) lifts this by letting
79	  the RTL lead the interrupt schedule and replaying it into QEMU.

108	## Usage 3: async-interrupt lock-step (`run --mode cycle --cosim --cosim-async`)
109	
110	The default lock-step (Usage 1) excludes async interrupts because each
111	engine runs on its own clock and takes the interrupt at a DIFFERENT attempt
112	index: QEMU is functional (no real cycles), the RTL is cycle-accurate, so
113	"the cycle the timer fires" maps to a different instruction on each side.
114	Aligning by attempt index then floods false divergences:
115	
116	```
117	QEMU:  998  999  [IRQ]-> handler ...               (took it at 1000)
118	RTL :  998  999  1000 ... 1499  [IRQ]-> handler     (took it at 1500)
119	                      ^ QEMU=handler vs RTL=mainloop -> false FAIL
120	```
121	
122	Fix (Dromajo's model): the cycle-accurate side LEADS, the functional oracle
123	FOLLOWS. The RTL owns CLINT/PLIC and decides when the interrupt is taken;
124	the oracle is TOLD to take the same cause at the same boundary and never
125	schedules its own. Dromajo exposes this as
126	`dromajo_cosim_raise_trap(state, hartid, cause)` ("DUT raises a trap and
127	provides the cause; MSB indicates an asynchronous interrupt"); andesim
128	does the equivalent by replaying the RTL's interrupt schedule into QEMU.
129	
130	Run order is INVERTED (RTL first); it is a register/CSR replay over the
131	existing two-pass + offline-diff structure:
132	
133	```
134	leg 1 (DUT leads):  vsim lock-step runs to program exit. After each
135	                    dcsr.step, mcause MSB set => an async IRQ was taken at
136	                    this attempt; record (attempt_index, cause).
137	leg 2 (oracle follows): QEMU replays bounded to K with the schedule
138	                    injected (raise cause at attempt_index, BEFORE that
139	                    instruction) and its own CLINT timer frozen.
140	diff:               record i vs i, exactly as Usage 1. Both entered the
141	                    handler at the same attempt => aligned, real bugs surface.
142	```
143	
144	andesim is easier here than a live SystemVerilog testbench: it reads the
145	RTL's COMMITTED mepc/mcause via DMI after each step, so it knows exactly
146	where the interrupt landed -- there is no speculative pipeline boundary to
147	negotiate (ImperasDV's pipeline-sync problem does not arise post-hoc).
148	
149	- Tradeoff: RTL-first loses the default's cheap "oracle fails fast on a bad
150	  ELF" property (Usage 1 runs the MHz oracle first). A hung DUT is bounded
151	  by `--cosim-max-records`.
152	- Opt-in: `--cosim-async`, default off (matches the F7 refine precedent);
153	  requires `--mode cycle --cosim`.
154	- WFI is free: the RTL stalls on WFI by its own timing, and the recorded
155	  schedule carries the wake interrupt that QEMU then replays.
156	- Periodic timers are free: the handler's mtimecmp rewrite is just normal
157	  compared instructions, and the next interrupt is again dictated by the
158	  RTL leg.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# run --mode cycle --cosim contract (cosim_redesign F6): lock-step DV co-sim.

# full record per execution attempt from the arm pc, and the streams are

#   1. self-initializing trap fixture, armed after init -> PASS (the ecall
#      traps round-trip identically; mcause/mepc compared and match)
#   2. a workload that relies on QEMU's boot-arg reset convention -> FAIL at
#      attempt 0 (the RTL resets GPRs to 0; the tool localizes it), rc 1
#   3. usage errors: fast model, --cosim-max-records gating
#   4. dev-only help surface
#
# Slow: each vsim step is a DMI single-step + full drain (~5s/record on
# ax45mpv). Bounded with --cosim-max-records to keep the gate to a few minutes.
set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
ROOT=$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/log.sh"
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/paths.sh"

BIN="$ROOT/build/andesim"
bash "$ROOT/scripts/build_driver.sh" >/dev/null 2>&1 || fail "build_driver.sh failed"

ENGINE="${ENGINE:-vsim:ax45mpv_premium}"
TRAP_ELF="$ROOT/tests/fixtures/rt_trap_ecall.elf"

[ -f "$TRAP_ELF" ] || fail "missing $TRAP_ELF (make -C tests/fixtures rt_trap_ecall.elf)"

      --pc-start roi_start --cosim-max-records 10 "$TRAP_ELF" 2>&1)

  || fail "trap: expected PASS with 10 records: $OUT"

      --cosim-max-records 2 "$HELLO_ELF" 2>&1)

printf '%s\n' "$OUT" | grep -Eq '\[cosim\] FAIL: first divergence at attempt 0' \

printf '%s\n' "$OUT" | grep -Eq 'pc +vsim=0x[0-9a-f]+ +qemu=0x[0-9a-f]+' \
  || fail "hello: divergence report missing both pcs: $OUT"
ok "cycle --cosim: divergence localized to the exact attempt with both pcs"

# 3. usage errors.
expect 2 'cosim requires --mode hybrid or cycle' \
  "$BIN" run --mode fast --cosim "$TRAP_ELF"
expect 2 'cosim-max-records requires --mode cycle --cosim' \
  "$BIN" run --mode hybrid --cosim-max-records 10 --engine "$ENGINE" "$TRAP_ELF"
ok "cycle --cosim usage errors (model / --cosim-max-records gating)"

# 4. dev-only help surface.

ok "run --mode cycle --cosim lock-step DV co-simulation"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Plugin cosim oracle mode (cosim_roi F3 + cosim_redesign F3): a pure-QEMU
# run arms at the ROI ENTRY boundary, then drains hybrid_state_v1 at
# caller-chosen post-entry retire counts: every count but the last APPENDS
# to the <outfile>.ckpts stream and keeps running; the LAST drains
# <outfile> and exits 200.
#
# Counting semantics (must mirror the vsim side's minstret deltas):
#   marker mode (cosim_marker=1): the ENTER marker is counted by NEITHER side
#     (QEMU1 drains pre-marker, vsim resumes past it). After count c, the
#     drained pc is the (c+1)-th insn after the marker.
#   pc mode (cosim_pc=0x...): the boundary insn retires INSIDE the window
#     (QEMU1's pc-mode handoff resumes AT the boundary), so it is retire #1.
#     After count c, the drained pc is the c-th insn counting the boundary
#     as #1... i.e. the insn at line offset c from the boundary line.
#
# Fixture: rt_c_v_regs -- its ROI is 7 straight-line V insns, so disasm line
# offsets equal dynamic retire order.
#
# Cases:
#   1. cosim_marker=1,cosim_counts=2:5:7 -> stream records 1/2 + final pc
#      + rc 200, stream holds exactly 2 records
#   2. cosim_pc=<enter>,cosim_counts=1:3 -> pc-mode counting (boundary = #1)
#   3. install errors: exclusive with other modes, counts required,
#      mode required for counts, counts strictly ascending.

set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/paths.sh"
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/roi.sh"

FIXTURE="${FIXTURE:-rt_c_v_regs}"
hybrid_resolve_paths

OBJDUMP="${OBJDUMP:-${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN:+$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-objdump}}"
OBJDUMP="${OBJDUMP:-riscv64-unknown-elf-objdump}"
command -v "$OBJDUMP" >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "skip[cosim_drain]: no objdump"; exit 77; }

DISASM=$("$OBJDUMP" -d "$VSIM_ELF")

MARKERS=$(roi_markers_from_disasm "$DISASM") \
  || { echo "FAIL[cosim_drain]: no ROI markers in $VSIM_ELF"; exit 1; }
ENTER_PC="0x${MARKERS%% *}"

# Address at disasm line offset d from the ENTER-marker line (straight-line
# ROI: line order == retire order).
pc_at() {
  printf '0x%s' "$(printf '%s\n' "$DISASM" | awk -v d="$1" '
    /5a002013/ { n = NR }
    n && NR == n + d { sub(/:$/, "", $1); print $1; exit }')"
}

STATE=$(mktemp)
QEMU_LOG=$(mktemp)
trap 'rm -f "$STATE" "$STATE".ckpt* "$QEMU_LOG"' EXIT

run_qemu() {  # $1 = plugin arg suffix (script runs without -e; RC checked per case)
  "$VSIM_QEMU" \
    -machine andes_ae350 \
    -cpu andes-ax45mpv,vlen=512 \
    -nographic \
    -semihosting-config enable=on,target=native \
    -bios "$VSIM_ELF" \
    -plugin "$VSIM_PLUGIN,outfile=$STATE,$1" \
    </dev/null >"$QEMU_LOG" 2>&1
  RC=$?
}

state_pc() {  # $1 = state file; prints 0x<pc>
  printf '0x%x' "0x$(od -A n -t x8 -j 16 -N 8 "$1" | tr -d ' ')"
}

# Record size = the final state file (exactly one hybrid_state_v1).
stream_pc() {  # $1 = stream file, $2 = 1-based record index; prints 0x<pc>
  RECSZ=$(stat -c %s "$STATE")
  printf '0x%x' \
    "0x$(od -A n -t x8 -j $(( ($2 - 1) * RECSZ + 16 )) -N 8 "$1" | tr -d ' ')"
}

check_pc() {  # $1 = case label, $2 = state file, $3 = want pc, [$4 = record]
  if [ ! -s "$2" ]; then
    echo "FAIL[cosim_drain]: $1: state file $2 missing"
    tail -5 "$QEMU_LOG"; exit 1
  fi
  if [ -n "${4:-}" ]; then GOT=$(stream_pc "$2" "$4"); else GOT=$(state_pc "$2"); fi

8	## Problem
9	
10	`--verify` (verify_oracle.md) compares only the FINAL state at the ROI exit.
11	When it fails, we know the vsim leg diverged somewhere inside the ROI, but not
12	where. Checkpoint co-sim drains and compares the architectural state every N

17	
18	```

20	                                  ckpt 1      ckpt 2      final drain
21	Run 2 (oracle):  pure QEMU from boot: arm at ROI entry, drain at the SAME
22	                 retire counts ->     ckpt 1      ckpt 2      final
23	diff ckpt k vs ckpt k (existing state_diff policy); first mismatch = window k.
24	```

27	instructions (halt slack, see verify_oracle.md "Boundary semantics"), and pc
28	alignment is ambiguous inside loops. vsim restores minstret from QEMU1's
